suggest.title: What the app suggests
suggest.pending: Answer the question about units and the app will tell you which scheme fits.
suggest.estratificada: Stratified: at random, keeping each class's share on both sides (for a quantity, each range of values).
suggest.grupo: By group: each unit lands whole on a single side.
suggest.tiempo: By time: the test set is your most recent dates, with a gap the size of your horizon before them.
suggest.tiempo-grupo: By time and by group: the test set is your most recent dates, and training leaves out the whole history of the units in it.
suggest.why-estratificada: Your stage 2 recorded neither a date nor a unit that repeats: there is no order or group to respect.
suggest.why-grupo: In your stage 2, the unit «{unidad}» repeats across rows: if the same unit lands on both sides, the model is evaluated on what it has already seen.
suggest.why-tiempo: In your stage 2 you recorded the date «{fecha}»: the model will use the past to decide what comes next, and the test set has to mimic that.
suggest.why-tiempo-grupo: You recorded a date and a unit that repeats, and said the model will be used with new units: the test set has to be in the future and made of units the model hasn't seen.
suggest.why-tiempo-conocidas: You recorded a date and a unit that repeats, and said the model will be used with the same units: it's enough for the test set to be in the future.

form.units: Will your model be used with new units or with the ones you already know?
form.units-help: With a date and a unit that repeats, the scheme depends on this, and the app can't know it.
form.units-nuevas: With new units the model hasn't seen
form.units-conocidas: With the same units, later in time
form.reason: Why do you choose a scheme other than the suggested one?
form.reason-help: It's kept in your notebook next to the suggested one.
form.size-help: A whole number between {min} and {max}; {sugerido} is suggested.
form.horizon: Horizon: how long until the outcome is known
form.horizon-help: That time is left as a gap between training and test. Write 0 if the outcome is known at the moment of deciding.

seal.title: Test set seal
seal.note: It comes from your data, the scheme, its parameters and which rows are the test set. If any of that changes, the seal doesn't match and stage 7 doesn't open. It's hygiene and traceability, not a promise: it says the test set is the same, not that nobody looked at it.
seal.count: Distinct test sets sealed in this notebook: {n}. Sealing a different one adds one: each different split is another way of looking.
seal.pending: The seal appears once the scheme and its parameters are complete.
